title: Drop support for pre-1.0 libpcap on non-Windows
description:
Require pcap_create(). That first appeared in libpcap 1.0, which
was released 2008-10-17. That also ensures that the entire libpcap
1.0 and earlier API is present, so we can remove some checks and
ifdefs.

On Windows the compile time checks have always been skipped and
the functions checked for at run time, so this really just removes
all the ifdefs but the run time checks are still there. A subsequent
commit could remove the run time checks and just refuse to load the
dll if pcap_create and other 1.0 APIs are not present.

Note WinPcap 4.1.3 fails to export three functions (pcap_statustostr(),
pcap_can_set_rfmon(), and pcap_set_rfmon()), so even if we do require
the rest of the libpcap 1.0 APIs on Windows, we might still want to mark
those as optional in Windows and work around their absence.

Ping #20261

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 5c7edfc6 - Drop support for pre-1.0 libpcap on non-Windows
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18629/diffs?diff_id=1223879512&start_sha=dacfe4656204a275f75a182f88d5ad2d3124ce5c)

> Note WinPcap 4.1.3 fails to export three functions (pcap_statustostr(), pcap_can_set_rfmon(), and pcap_set_rfmon()), so even if we do require the rest of the libpcap 1.0 APIs on Windows, we might still want to mark those as optional in Windows and work around their absence.

WinPcap doesn't support monitor mode, so, if we don't find `pcap_can_set_rfmon()`, we can fall back on built-in code that says "no", and if we don't find `pcap_set_rfmon()`, we can fall back on built-in code that returns 0 (not ideal) or that has a definition of WinPcap 4.1.3's `pcap_t` structure and sets the rfmon flag (runs the risk of randomly stomping on the structure if we're *not* using 4.1.3).

For `pcap_statustostr()`, we could fall back on a routine that uses the libpcap 1.0 `pcap_statustostr()` list of errors.
Is there any reason to keep supporting WinPcap?

> Is there any reason to keep supporting WinPcap?

The only reasons that come to mind are

1. supporting versions of Windows on which Npcap doesn't work;
2. I seem to remember some people having, at one point, issues with Npcap fixed by installing Winpcap.

Given that, according to [the LifeCycle page on the Wireshark Wiki](https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/LifeCycle), Wireshark 4.*2* was the last release to support Windows *10*, 1) is not a valid reason for continuing to support WinPcap in anything remotely resembling a recent release.

2) *might* be, but I think it's been a while since I've seen those issues, so maybe that one's not worth it, either.

So maybe we drop support for it.  We may still want to make the routines in question optional, so that we can *load* WinPcap sufficiently to ask for its version string and report to the user "sorry, we no longer support WinPcap" if they try to use Wireshark with WinPcap.

I remember some issues along the line of "you installed NPcap without uninstalling WinPcap properly, and Wireshark loaded a WinPcap DLL instead of NPcap," for which the "sorry, we found WinPcap" message might be useful.

> Is there any reason to keep supporting WinPcap?

The Fedora supplies MinGW package of WinPcap (https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/mingw-wpcap/) but not npcap. That's used as the SDK when cross-compiling - at runtime, whatever's actually installed on a system, like NPcap is used. So we do need to keep defining `HAVE_REMOTE` for that case.
